title: AgentManifest
description: The contract every capability declares about itself. The ten fields required by Rule 3 are required keys here, so a manifest that omits one fails validation, which fails CI. This is how Rule 3 is enforced by machine rather than by review.

version.description: Semver. Minor bump = prompt or model change. Major bump = I/O schema change.

kind.description: agent = makes a model call. connector = deterministic, no model call. hybrid = deterministic tool then model interpretation.

purpose.description: Rule 3, field 1. One paragraph stating what this does AND what it does not do.

nonResponsibilities.description: Explicit anti-scope. Feeds the duplicate-responsibility lint (Rule 4). Strongly encouraged.

inputs.description: Rule 3, field 3. JSON Schema for the input. This is the interface.

outputs.description: Rule 3, field 4. JSON Schema for the output. This is the interface.

memory.description: Rule 3, field 5. May be empty, must be present. The orchestrator resolves exactly these scopes into an immutable snapshot; a capability cannot read outside them.

tools.description: Rule 3, field 6. Capability ids of connectors this may call. An explicit allowlist — empty means pure reasoning with no side effects.

credentials.description: Secret scopes resolved at call time. FORBIDDEN when kind is 'agent' (see the allOf constraint below). Credentials are never read into memory, prompts, or logs.

prompt.description: Rule 3, field 7. Path to a versioned prompt file, or null for connectors. Prompt files are immutable once shipped; improving one means adding vN+1.

impl.description: Path to the typed implementation. Required for connectors.

failureConditions.description: Rule 3, field 8. Retry behavior is derived from these plus the error taxonomy, never guessed.

when.description: Human-readable condition; evaluated by the runner or asserted in tests.

to.description: Escalation target capability id. Required when action is 'escalate'.

successConditions.description: Rule 3, field 9. Human-readable. The eval suite scores real output against these.

dependencies.description: Rule 3, field 10. Capability ids. Lint-enforced to resolve and to stay acyclic.

model.description: Execution profile. Names a TIER, never a model id — so re-pointing every capability at a new model is a one-line config change and no manifest mentions a vendor.

allOf.$comment: Agents make model calls, so they must have a prompt and must NOT declare credentials. This is the schema-level enforcement of the boundary in ADR-0005: an agent has no path to a secret.
Connectors are deterministic: no prompt, no model profile, and an implementation pointer instead.
Hybrids interpret tool output with a model, so they need both a prompt and at least one tool.

memoryScope.description: e.g. brand.tone, brand.guidelines, content.winning_hooks, content.rejected_ideas, metrics.engagement
